prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat electronic bands in twisted bilayer graphene at a magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in this tunable moire system

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep B017 as my preferred configuration, but with a narrower claim than I made before. What I would reward is the existence of a tunable flat-band correlated platform: the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model gave a specific, checkable prediction that the bandwidth collapses at a magic twist angle, and the 2018 experiments in Jarillo-Herrero's group showed correlated insulating and superconducting states tuned by twist angle and gate voltage. The claim is not a theory of the superconducting pairing, which remains open and which the citation should not assert. The three credited names map onto the structure of that sequence (prediction, then experiment) without an arbitrary cut, which is not true of B010, B042 or B003. Reproduction by several independent groups and extension to other stacks over eight years is, in my judgement, a normal horizon for a condensed-matter discovery, and as an electronic-structure theorist I weigh heavily that computed band structure and measured transport meet so directly. I also want to be explicit that I have no objection to B001 as the sole prize. Six colleagues who know the science of the clocks better than I do describe it as secure, independently confirmed and cleanly credited, and I find that credible. My preference for B017 is a judgement that a discovery of a new regime of correlated matter weighs somewhat more than an instrument-driven advance, not a claim that the clocks fail any test.
statement.case_against: The reservations against B017 are real and round 1 sharpened them. The eight-year age and the unsettled pairing mechanism make the field younger than the clocks, as Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson and Johansson all say. Attribution is the weaker side: Yuan Cao, first author of the 2018 papers, Dean, Young, Kim, Yacoby, Efetov and others are outside the three names, and relying on the group-leader convention for the experiment is defensible but open to criticism. By comparison the B001 credit has the smallest gap on the shortlist, and the overlap with 1989, 2005 and 2012 appears to be mostly a presentational matter that a carefully worded citation can handle. I have also lowered my view of B015, which I listed as an alternative in round 1, because Danielsson, Kroll, Mehlig and Olsson each pointed to the unresolved Miyazaki, Moodera, Parkin and Yuasa credit and to the 2007 GMR prize; I no longer think it is a robust fallback. Finally, B017 has the support of two of eight members, and the committee should not choose it merely because I regard it as the more interesting science.

responses.point: Kroll asked whether the unresolved attribution questions in my top choices weigh as much as the overlap concerns raised against the clocks, since he sees the clock configuration as the cleaner of the two.
responses.response: On attribution alone I agree: the Katori and Ye configuration is cleaner than mine, and I said so in round 1. I weigh the two concerns differently, though. The overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes is something the citation can answer by naming the lattice clock and the magic-wavelength concept, and you, Lindroth, Mehlig and Olsson have convinced me it is not a bar. The omission of Cao and other moire groups cannot be repaired by wording, but it is the ordinary consequence of the three-person limit in a fast field, and the Nobel record has several such cases. So my answer is that B001 is the safer prize and B017 the one I find scientifically more compelling, and I would accept B001 without objection if that is where the committee lands. Your point that B017 lacks the maturity of clocks confirmed in national laboratories is fair, and I only dispute that it is a decisive point.

responses.point: Olsson says B017 would be more convincing in a year or two once the pairing mechanism and experimental credit are better settled, and that she would move it up if the field were judged secure enough now.
responses.response: I think the first half of that depends on what is being rewarded. If the mechanism of superconductivity were the discovery, waiting would make sense. What is established now is the flat-band platform and the existence of correlated insulating and superconducting phases, reproduced by multiple groups as functions of twist angle and gating. Pairing is a downstream question, as it was for the cuprates. The experimental credit, by contrast, will not become clearer with time, since the first-author and group-leader question will be the same next year. I also take her point on B015: I conceded it already and have now dropped it from my alternatives. I accept that waiting a year costs the committee little, so if she and colleagues prefer that, I would not call it unreasonable, but I would ask that the committee decide on the grounds of what is rewarded and not on the unsolved mechanism.

responses.point: Mehlig regards B017 as a rare theory-experiment sequence but would make it the first alternative, and judges that eight years is short compared with clocks reproduced by independent laboratories.
responses.response: I agree with the description of B017 as a rare theory-to-experiment sequence and I accept that the clocks have a longer record of independent confirmation. Eight years is shorter, but several groups have independently reproduced the correlated insulators and superconducting domes in twisted bilayer graphene, and the same flat-band mechanism has been realised in other stacks, which is the kind of replication that matters for a discovery. I disagree that Cao's absence makes the three names unworkable; I think we must name the omission openly in any public statement, and I will not argue that the group-leader convention removes the difficulty. Where I now agree with him is on B010: its allocation among Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Hasan and the uncredited Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal is too unstable, and I therefore list it as an alternative only because the core credit is less unstable than the others.

responses.point: Danielsson says he cannot judge from outside the field whether the clocks are distinct from 2005 and 2012, and qualified my enthusiasm for B015 as unresolved on credit.
responses.response: On B015 you are right and I have moved: I put it in my round-1 alternatives, and after reading you, Kroll, Mehlig and Olsson I think its credit and the 2007 overlap leave it weaker than B010, where the Kane and Molenkamp core is at least clearer. On the clocks, the atomic-physics members have answered your question from the inside: Lindroth, Kroll and Olsson argue that the comb is the readout tool and the lattice clock a separate problem, and I think that answer is persuasive enough that you and I can treat the overlap as a matter for the citation. That leaves us with B017 as a position we hold on scientific weight, and I agree we should word it narrowly around flat bands and correlated states so that fractional Chern insulators and later moire discoveries are left for another year.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will treat the unresolved pairing mechanism as a question of maturity or as separate from the discovery being rewarded.
Whether the omission of Cao and other moire-device groups can be defended publicly under the three-person limit, and whether the group-leader convention is enough.

How much weight the near-consensus on B001 among members with direct expertise in precision measurement should carry against my own view that B017 is the stronger discovery; I cannot judge the metrology details myself and I have tried not to count heads in place of science.
My recollection of twisted-bilayer history, including earlier band-structure work on twisted bilayers and the priority of the flat-band idea, is from memory and not verified against sources.
statement.conflict_note: No documented personal or institutional tie to any credited person on B017, B001 or B010 appears in my profile. My research in electronic structure, DFT and magnetism is adjacent to B017 and B015, which is familiarity and not a conflict, and the committee should discount my enthusiasm for B017 accordingly. I do not disclose any further tie after reading the other members' disclosures.
